utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I hope that everyone was duly informed that we'll try to finish the videolink material today. That means that I urge the parties to examine the witnesses as efficiently as possible, but that might be a repetitious request. But first of all, we still have to give decisions on the admission into evidence of the documents tendered yesterday. Madam Registrar, could you please assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yesterday, for the Defence -- for the OTP, we have two documents need to be admitted. One is P3279W, and 3266.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And P3279W is a --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Is a CD-ROM showing the home and -- Ms. Pita's home and where her daughter was shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the CD-ROM.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And P3266 is the photo of a tree seen from the porch of Ms. Pita's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They are both admitted in evidence. Then we have Defence documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think the CD-ROM is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was re-tendered, yes. I think it's the same one as has been shown to Mr. Pita when he testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that would be repetitious to -- no, I have -- it's a different one. Is it slightly different? Yes, then my earlier decision stands. But looking at your list, we have 3280W. It's newly tendered. I see on the list 3280W, and 3266. I think the first one -- we had a video with Mrs. Pita.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, yes, 3280W is the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the video -- so that's new. And that's, then, admitted in evidence. And 3266 is the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D74 still remains to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And D74, Madam Registrar, is?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's a document concerning military activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the part of Annex 6 of the report of the committee of experts. That's admitted into evidence as well. Let me then check with Sarajevo whether we have a good image and sound link with Sarajevo. Yes, I do not have it yet on my screen. Yes, I have got it. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. In an agreement procedure with which Mr. Ierace spoke yesterday, I wish to inform you that I have to be in Geneva tonight at 1900 so that I will have to leave earlier, and I will not be able to be present here until the end of today's hearing. For that reason, we believe that it would be better if the Defence raised now a problem which has to do with exhibits which were -- will be presumably introduced with the two witnesses, and we have a motion to make in this regard. Does the Chamber allow us to do it right now? It will take five minutes on my part, Your Honour. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, do it just as efficiently as possible, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I will now need the help of the usher. Usher [In English], with of course the authorisation of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've prepared three sets of documents, Mr. President, which all have to do with the witness, Ramiza Kundo. These documents are in the original language, that is the Serbian language, plus English translation. You will see this is a very important factor. These need to be distributed. And there is one more copy, one free copy here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's quite unusual to distribute them all, but let's just see what you tell us about these sets of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I shall be happy to do that. May I do it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. President, the first set of documents has the number 0028-4046. This document has to do once again with the medical documentation. I believe a letter of discharge, the number of which is 47, and I took the liberty to mark it in a coloured marker so we can see, and later on you see document 48, which is only the certificate. Mr. President, if we look at two other sets of documents which I've underlined in pink here and there and others in blue, you will see something which is the translation of that same document, but once again in two different versions of this translation. And you will see that what is here underlined very clearly is what exists in one document but does not exist in the other one. So this is the thick line. What is a dotted line, these are the indications which were included in this form and one can find them in one translation and not in another one. And we are not able to see why. But the thing which is most upsetting, which is of greatest concern, other documents were given to the Defence and we wonder why. If you locate, Mr. President, Document Number -- ending in figures 47.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what I assume is that you are protesting against translations that are not correct or not reflecting what is in the original language, and that there are two different -- or it's not that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not only, Mr. President. What I wish to simply say, and I will endeavour to be as brief as possible, in the translation which I underlined in pink so that everyone can see clearly, there is only one page which was translated, and that is the page which I marked in pink and which bears the signature of Dr. Ivanisevic. This is a page that does not exist in the original, I mean these practically we do not have even two identical documents. And Mr. President, if we take the original, then you will see that the signature, one of the doctors, is that of Dr. F. There is no doubt about that, a capital "F." And then I cannot read it, because it is not properly reproduced, but it ends in "novic." In the translation that we have, and that is the pink one, the pink translation, we see that this "F" has become "Faruk." I do not know how one can arrive at that on the basis of one initial because it could have been Farid, Franjo, Franko, whatever. And you will also see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, these are, I would say, at first sight, wholly justified remarks on invented parts of the document. That's, as a matter of fact, what I was talking about two minutes ago. Let's do it the following way: The Prosecution is, I think, very well aware that this Chamber is not very much inclined to accept any documents where the translation gives far more information than the original document and is therefore not a true and proper translation of the original text. I'm quite certain that Mr. Ierace is fully aware of -- was fully aware of this problem yesterday, so I do expect that he will today either explain to us why such documents do exist or withdraw any translations, or will not tender documents or will tender them with a certain explanation. So I think we could at this moment proceed and wait and see what Mr. Ierace does, and he's aware of the problem, I'm certain. Is that true, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What the Defence wishes is to formally apply to the Chamber formally, in line with Rule 92 -- 98 of the Rules of Procedure because, as I said, "Faruk" could be "Franjo," could be whatever, so that the Prosecution then is issued an order by your Chamber to produce only integral and original medical documentation because the Defence wastes considerable time to check all these documents. And we are requesting this for the medical documentation, but the same holds true of the documents of military nature which we shall be having. As of today, Defence wishes to be able to work normally. So with all due respect, we are making this application. The Prosecution should be ordered to submit the -- only the original of the documents and nothing else, and this goes for the medical and military documents alike. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, Rule 98 deals with the production of additional evidence, and therefore I think the system should be that we first wait and see what the evidence is which will be adduced by the Prosecution, and then we'll see. And we took notice of your request that if this was the evidentiary material produced by the Prosecution, that you'd like us to order the Prosecution to produce additional evidence, especially the original documents, medical documentation. Mr. Ierace, you are aware of the problem, I think. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, certainly I'm aware that there are two copies of each of the medical reports. I have some trouble in following some of the concerns of Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Others, I understand. I will lead evidence from the next witness as to the nature of medical treatment that she received, and the places from which she received it. And I propose that the concerns that Mr. Piletta-Zanin has, since they go to admissibility and since that is the thrust of his request, be dealt with at the conclusion of her evidence. I suspect that Mr. Piletta-Zanin has a sufficiently legible copy of each of the medical documents which have been disclosed to him to conduct his cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first proceed and see where we are at the end of the examination of the witness. Ms. Philpott.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. I take it that you can understand us and that you can see us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the next witness you want to call is?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ramiza Kundo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ramiza Kundo. Could you please bring Ramiza Kundo into the videoroom in Sarajevo, Ms. Philpott.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Kundo -- I now see two markers. Could we just have on our video -- Ms. Philpott, we have two marker pens. No, I think we now have again the image of Ms. Kundo and you, Ms. Philpott. Ms. Kundo, good morning, welcome, although at a distance in what you could consider to be the courtroom in Sarajevo. Before giving testimony in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you now by the representative of the Registry. May I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mrs. Kundo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, from your reactions, I take it that you can hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll be examined by, first, counsel for the Prosecution and you'll then be examined by counsel for the Defence. So I'll first now give the opportunity to Mr. Ierace to start your examination as a witness. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Kundo, would you please give your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: My name is -- my name is Ramiza Kundo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: 16th of April, 1955.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you lived in Sarajevo since 1965?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Since when?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Since --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the technicians either in Sarajevo or in The Hague take care that the sound is ... You now can hear us again, Ms. Kundo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you live in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Since when have you lived in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Since 1965.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you married with two children?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Between 1992 and 1995, where in Sarajevo did you live?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: In Brijesce, and that is where I still live.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what sort of building were you living in Brijesce in those years?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: In my house, brick house. We built it before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During the war, did your house suffer any damage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: It did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What caused that damage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Shells and those shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what years during the war did your house suffer that damage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: In the beginning of the war, 1992, in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How far from your house was the confrontation line or confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, about a kilometre, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On what side of the confrontation lines was your house? In other words, which forces controlled the area where you lived?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't understand. I don't know. Serb, Serb troops, Serb army, Serb police, they were there, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In terms of the armed forces during the conflict, which armed forces controlled the area -- withdraw that question. Which forces were on the other side of the confrontation -- which forces were on the other side of the confrontation line from where you lived?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Our side. Our army, but in the early days, there was no army. There was nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were the forces on the other side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: The Serbs were, the Serb army. The Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During the war, did your house have any running water?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No, we didn't. We were getting the water from the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How did you receive the water from the city?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, before the war, there was the city water supply. And then later on, we had to go to various springs when they cut off the -- when they cut it off, when we had no more water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there a particular spring that you would go to, to get water for your house?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: There were several places.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During the war, were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On what date did that happen?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: It was the 2nd of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were you doing at the time that you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I had gone to fetch water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did anyone go with you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, a woman was with me, Rasema Menzilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What time was it when you went to get water?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I think - I'm not quite sure - but I think it was sometime in early afternoon. It could have been around 4.00 or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the weather like at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Cloudy, overcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that you went to get water. How far away from your home was the place that you were going to get the water, approximately?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: About 50 metres or so. Water from my house, about 20 metres, because there was the main road which we had to cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the source of the water? Was it a creek or a spring or something else?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: A spring.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, get some water from the spring?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, and on my way back, when we were about to run across the road, the sniper hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How were you carrying the water? What was it in?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: In a canister, in 10-litre canisters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How did you cross the road? Were you walking or running or what?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how I was moving exactly at that particular time but I'm sure that I was hurrying. I wasn't walking leisurely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What actually happened as you crossed road? What did you feel? What did you hear? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I heard the shot. When I was hit, I thought it was a stone, a pebble, which had hit me and then I hurried even more. I just hastened to cross the road. I felt the pain, and then I pulled up my trouser leg and I saw some blood. And then I pulled it down again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which of your legs was hit?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: The left one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts on your leg?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Below the knee.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: The calf, the bullet went through.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. At the time that you were shot, do you know where Rasema Menzilovic was? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: She was with me. I don't know if she was in front of me or behind me. I don't know. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear any sound at about the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I heard the shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where did you hear the sound of the shot come from? Was it from straight ahead, from behind you, or from one of your sides?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: It came from the right, as I was moving, from -- about from Serbian lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What happened after you were shot? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Rasema went to fetch some men to take me over there, to fetch the men who were for the civilian -- how do you call them -- to save me, to take me to the hospital. She went to get a car to come and fetch me. I went to the hospital. They cleaned the wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were you wearing at that time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I was wearing a long skirt and a shirt and a pullover. I always wore such clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What colour was the skirt?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I think it was violet. It was colourful.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that you were taken to the hospital. What hospital was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: It was in Kosevo. I don't know which street it was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How long did you stay there for?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: For three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time that you were shot, did you see anyone nearby?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you see any military vehicles nearby or military equipment?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What about military equipment?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that a video be shown. The Exhibit Number of the video is 3280V.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, in a few minutes you will see a video on the screen in front of you. Please look at it carefully. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, can you confirm that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Yes, Your Honour. We have it on the screen, but it's not as clear as it has been in the past this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the quality is not sufficient, please inform us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you please show me, to the best of your recollection, where the corner of the garage used to be at the time you were shot. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will now mark that location using yellow spray paint. "I have put a yellow line and a number 1. "Mrs. Kundo, could you now show me, stand where you were located, to the best of your recollection, at the time you were shot. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will now mark that spot using yellow spray paint. "I've marked it with a yellow X with a number 1 beside it. "Mrs. Kundo, could you please face in the direction that you were facing and assume the position that you were as close as you can -- as you can recall, at the time that you were shot. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: And finally, can you please indicate from which direction you heard the gunshot, as closely as you can recall, at the time that you were shot. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates]"

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you comply with the requests of the investigator truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it. On the video, we saw the investigator ask you to do certain things, to point in certain directions according to your recollection, and to stand in certain places according to your recollection. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you did those things, were you truthful, according to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I think that I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you will now see a photograph on the screen. As soon as the photograph appears, can you tell us that you can see it. The photograph should show a street with a tree and some shrubs on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. President, this is Exhibit Number P3279V.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to see a photograph on the screen, Mrs. Kundo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what appears in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is it? What do you see?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: A street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the name of that street?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Brijesce Brdo Cikma.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does it have a new name now?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, Bulbulistan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, please assume that the position that you told the investigator as where you were shot is also the position from which this photograph was taken. Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. We will now move the photograph slowly to the right. Stop for a minute, please. At the moment you were shot, were you crossing from the left-hand side of the road as we look at the photograph to the right-hand side, or were you crossing from the right-hand side to the left-hand side? Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I was coming back with the water. I was returning home. And that was around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. So in what direction did you cross the road at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Towards the house. I was crossing the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean by that, you were crossing from the left to the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel is speaking over the witness so we cannot hear him. We are sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you said has not been translated. You said it's a leading question. In what respect, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think -- I want to be brief for the sake of the witness. But I think that the fact of saying that you were crossing from left to right or right to left and to formulate it in this manner, I think that this is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What other ways of crossing the road are there, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? If the witness has testified that she crossed the road, it must be from one side to the other or from the other side to the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can say that -- I could tell you how the question should be formed. For example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. If you cross a road, you go from one side to the other side. So it's from the left to the right or from the right to left if the road is there. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it assists you, in the interests of time, I'm happy to withdraw the question and rephrase it. I'm mindful of the time difficulties we have today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would deny the objection. But if you want to rephrase it, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, you've just told us that -- excuse me. Mrs. Kundo, you've just told us that at the time that you were shot, you were crossing the road towards the house. Is that the house that appears on the right-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Towards the house, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it the one which appears on the right-hand side --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: You can see it up above. My garage is there. But I had to pass below.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. So if I can just ask you this question, to be clear: When you say "towards the house," was the house on the right-hand side of the photograph, somewhere in that area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know, really, whether that was on the left or the right side. I can't find my way around. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's all right. We will continue to move the photograph to the right, slowly.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: How can I explain where I was passing through? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, do you recognise the two buildings which appear in the photograph at the moment?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript, Mr. President, the screen shows two buildings. The one on the right has a pitched roof; the one on the left has a glass front, solid columns facing the street, and what appears to be a box on the pavement near the doorway, a number of sections in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, did either of these buildings exist at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No. Garages were there. There was a house but it was destroyed, and another one has been built: The one that you can see on the screen right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where was the garage in relation to your home at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: On the same side as my house. That's where the garage was. Maybe 20 metres further up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Given those answers, it seems that as you crossed the road, when you were shot, were you facing towards this direction, towards the garage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will continue to move the photograph to the right. Having regard to your earlier answer, what we see now was on your right side as you crossed the road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From the photograph, it appears that the road drops steeply as you move towards the hills. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Beyond the road, according to the photograph, we seem to be able to see a flat green area and a valley with a lot of buildings in it. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is that area immediately at the bottom of the hill?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: We call it the Serbian field. The Serbian lines were down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will continue to move the photograph to the right. Are you able to see in the photograph now the path from which you were returning from the spring?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript, Mr. President, the photograph shows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we didn't hear the witness identify the path that she took when she was bringing the water. I think that my colleague is suggesting to the witness that she should confirm that that is the path she took when she was bringing the water. I think that the witness should first identify the route she took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the line of questioning is -- I don't know what line exactly you're referring to, whether a question put by the Prosecutor has not been answered. If there's any additional information you would need or if you think the questioning is unfair, for whatever reason, you may object against that. Well, what information the Prosecution seeks to obtain from the answers of the witness is entirely up to the Prosecution, and in cross-examination of course you can seek whatever additional information you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Shall I continue, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. I merely wish to record the image which appears on the screen at the moment. There is a mound of a whitish material along the side of the road, and that is slightly to the right of centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will now continue to move the photograph slowly to the right. Stop there, please. Do you recognise what appears in the photograph now, Mrs. Kundo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to indicate to us where you began to cross the road at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Can you see this little hill?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: That's where I was crossing, towards the garage. That's where I was crossing the road. How shall I put it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By "little hill," do you mean the white pile which is not too far from the bitumen?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's sand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mrs. Kundo, you told us you were married. Where was your husband that day?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: He was in hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like the witness to see a document. It is part of Exhibit P1800 and it bears ERN number 0028-4047. Perhaps a copy could be shown to the witness in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, could you please give the requested document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] If Mr. Ierace could please repeat the ERN number. This document has three pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, and whilst this is being done, Mr. President, perhaps it could be distributed here as well. It is the second page, if it helps, of P1800. The ERN number appears at the bottom of the page. It's 0028-4047.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have objections with regard to this document, but I suggest that we make them later so as not to lose time. And I will remain silent, but this is an exception. It is not because I ought to keep quiet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I never urge you to keep quiet. I always urge you to work as efficient as possible, and you're doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is there now a document before you, Mrs. Kundo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: The discharge letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you first see that letter?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: When they discharged me from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you still have the original of that document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't have it with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you give a copy of that document, or did you hand it for a short time to an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what year was that? In what year did you do that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, did you sign some statements that were made to investigators from the Prosecutor's office? I'll repeat that question. I didn't have my microphone on. Mrs. Kundo, did you sign some statements that you made to investigators of the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like a document to be placed on the ELMO at this end. I don't have copies ready. It relates to an issue which arose this morning. I have one copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would perhaps first show the copy of the document to the Defence so that they know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give it to the Defence so that they can identify it more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand that the interpreters have copies of this document, Mr. President. I have one other spare copy, if that would assist you, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the translators, the interpreters' booth, have no copies. Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my case manager gave them some copies this morning, and I think, going on the nods I can see through the glass, they have now located them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we seem to have the copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If it would assist, I don't wish to state the date at this stage, but the witness will shortly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's first see how we can proceed even under these circumstances. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the document be placed on the ELMO here so that the bottom part of the document is visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have received this document. I would like to thank the Prosecution. I would like to draw your attention to the fact -- to a document. I don't know if it is this one but it resembles the document that was mentioned, P1800, but it's not the same, because it contains certain other elements. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first see what happens, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With great interest, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you put it on the ELMO, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'd like the document be placed on the ELMO so that we can see the bottom part. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, can you see on your screen at the moment a document which has some signatures?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of the signatures?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I recognise mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember why you placed your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I was making a statement about my being wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I ask the document be turned to page 4. That's ERN number, last four numbers, 0641, and that the top part of the document be displayed bearing her signature and the date. Perhaps the top part could be shown. A bit further. More of the top. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, do you recognise your name on the screen on the document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you write your name there and did you write the date?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In other words, did you sign this document on the 4th of May, 2001?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the last page of the document, ERN number 0643, which appears to be a photocopy of another document, be placed on the screen and that the bottom part of that document be displayed, the last line in particular. Perhaps the document could be moved up. Further, further. And then we could zoom in on the last line. Perhaps the document could be moved up further. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, again, do you recognise your name and the same date handwritten on the bottom of the screen?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you write your name and the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document? And we will zoom it back -- we will show you more of the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could the document be drawn down the screen so that more is visible. A little further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document, Mrs. Kundo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I do. It is my letter of discharge from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that a photograph be placed on the ELMO. Exhibit P1811, and a copy of the photograph be shown to the witness in Sarajevo. To assist you, Ms. Philpott, the photograph shows a two-storey building, plus ground, with some black lines on it, in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott [sic], do you recognise this photograph? Mrs. Kundo, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What does it show?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, it shows a building and that car and the crossing, the road. This is the main road, and that is the road that we had to cross coming back with water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I think you said earlier that there was a garage in that area which is no longer there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you place some lines, some black marks, on this photograph in October last year?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I didn't. That man who came, Robert, he did that. And he took those shots, and he crossed -- drew those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So your evidence is that you did not place these black lines on the photograph. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm sorry, but since I was on the other channel, I heard saying not only "Robert," but perhaps "Robert Barry." That is what I believe I heard from the booth. Now I don't know. It doesn't appear in the English transcript, but that is what I heard from the -- from another booth, namely, that is the French booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm certain proper care will be taken to make sure that the transcript reflects what has been said. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that another document be placed on the ELMO. Again, I haven't provided copies, haven't obtained copies for you, Mr. President and Your Honours. But in any event, I'd seek to have the document placed on the ELMO. Perhaps it could be shown to the Defence first so they can identify it. It's a document that has ERN number 0212-4042.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I do understand that these documents. Also the documents of which -- the five-page document you earlier gave the ERN numbers, what -- could you please renumber them as well? Because they have not the usual pre-numbering. So even if you haven't done it yet, then perhaps during the next break that you'll take care that we have the numbers you'd like to attribute to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the documentation of the Prosecution, I don't know if they are aware of this, but what I see here are certain markings which were not indicated, which were done in pencil, and we do not know whether this was done by the witness or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the documents are shown to you so that you know what documents are presented by the Prosecutor. The Prosecutor will then ask questions about it. And as we have seen with the differences on the -- what seems to be discharge form, let's just have the Prosecutor proceed. And it's not up to you at this moment to initiate any debate on the content of the document. It's shown to you so that you can identify the document. And of course, then later if you -- during cross-examination or when objecting against the admission in evidence, we can then see. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might that document be returned to me before it's placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in view of Mr. Piletta-Zanin's concern about pencil marks, I've obliterated part of the text, if he wishes to view it again to make sure before it's placed on the ELMO. Otherwise, we can simply place it straight on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'd like to inspect it again, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We shall see it during the cross-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the document be placed on the ELMO at the page which it is presently opened at. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, again, do you recognise your signature on a document on the ELMO, the document before you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Could you zoom it in, please, closer. Kundo. No, this is not me -- oh, no, it is. It is. It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. When you signed it, did you also place the date that you signed it on the document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that the 30th of October, 2001?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what I see. I can't remember all that, but yes, that's what I see, the 30th of October. Right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the -- I might have access again to the document briefly. For the record, the page just placed on the ELMO had ERN number 0212-4043. I now ask that the following page be placed on the ELMO so the witness can see the top half. And could we zoom in so that the top part, that is, the part just above the signature, is legible. Please stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to read the words on the screen now, Mrs. Kundo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, I can read this where it says -- where it shows my name. And you mean the 30th of October? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you place your name on that document on that date?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I did. Yes, I recognise my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'd be grateful if we could move the document very slightly to the left, just a centimetre or so. If we could move the document to the left. A bit too far. Back a bit. And could we zoom in so as to maximize -- yes, back a bit. Please stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, could you please read out the words above your signature, and please read them slowly.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I can't see a thing. "Witness's acknowledgment." I don't have glasses. I can't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Mrs. Kundo, before you signed your statements, were they read to you by an interpreter so that they were interpreted into Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you check that the statement was correct by listening to the interpreter before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the document be returned to me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you signed that document on the 30th of October, 2001, do you remember these words being read to you by an interpreter: "I previously provided a statement to the ICTY about the incident in which I was wounded by a sniper bullet. Today, I have examined a photograph showing the location where I was at the time, and I am marking on the photograph in black marker the position of the garage which was there at the time but has since been moved. I am also marking in black marker the new structures which were not present at the time I was wounded. I am signing the photograph, and it is to be attached to this statement." Does that, to the best of your recollection -- is that, to the best of your recollection, the contents of a statement that you signed on that date?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is your recollection now as to who made the black marks on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I remember, yes, Robert Barry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this -- Mrs. Pilipovic will take on the first stage, but as I have already said in the beginning, I believe that towards the end of Mrs. Pilipovic's cross-examination, I will also rise in order to address questions of translations of documents and all the rest of it, as I have indicated, of course with your permission, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I will give leave to split up the cross-examination. Mrs. Kundo, you'll now be examined by counsel for the Defence. Please, Ms. Pilipovic, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Kundo.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that in relation to the incident which you tell us happened on the 2nd of November, 1993, that you gave two statements to OTP investigators, on the 4th of May, 2001 and on the 30th of October, 2001?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I know that I gave statements when they came to my home and asked me questions. But when was it, I really don't know because all those dates and things.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that what you said to OTP investigators was included in the statement that you signed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, you told us that on the 2nd of November, 1993, the incident happened around 4.00 in the afternoon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- that incident which happened on the 2nd of November, 1993, did you go and report that incident to some authority? When I say "authority," I mean the police.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if any of your family, with reference to the incident that happened to you, gave a statement to any relevant authority in relation to the incident which happened to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, my husband did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when did your husband make a statement and before whom?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't know. He was summoned to the Court. But who that was, I don't know. I even didn't know why they were summoning him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you confirming to us that that day, when the incident happened, your husband was not at home?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He was in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that your husband was a member of the 2nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: He was with the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where were the positions of the army that your husband belonged to?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, they were across the road. Now, I don't know -- I don't know exactly, but they were out of the locality, out of the neighbourhood, beyond it. Beyond the road, down there. Our lines mainly went along the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far were what you call your lines away from your house?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, it could have been 500 metres. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to your lines where your husband was, too, and you tell us that they were 500 metres away in relation to your house, how far were the positions of the army of Republika Srpska in relation to your house or, as you put it, the Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, I would say a thousand metres, kilometre something. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that in relation to your house, first came the positions of the BH army, and then behind the positions of the BH army, that there were the positions of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of a uniform did your husband have?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, in the early days, they had their own uniforms. I mean, they wore their own civilian clothes. But, later on, they were issued with their uniforms, but I would say it was rather towards the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was your husband issued with a weapon, and what kind of a weapon did he have?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He had nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you answer how many -- how much time did your husband spend at the position during a week or a day?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't really know exactly what kind of shifts they had. Perhaps two or three days he would be away. He distributed food. He never went to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that in 1992, 1993, 1994, in the area in which you lived, if there were armed conflicts between the BH army and the army of Republika Srpska, or to make matters simpler, whether there was any fighting and gunfire in the area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to who opened fire in that fighting? Did both sides open fire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I know the Serbs opened fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how often did that happen, with what frequency?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I don't. I know snipers never stopped firing at us, and they shelled, and our men were only on the line or by the line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge when you say "yours," you mean the army -- the troops of the army of BH?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did yours -- did yours return the fire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, on the basis of what knowledge are you telling us that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Because I know that ours did not -- that our folk did not open fire. We know that, but we knew when the Serbs fired at us, because ours did not have any weapons or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the neighbourhood, in the vicinity of where you live, where your house is, is there a church there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: A church? Yes. Above me, could be some 500 metres uphill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us, in that area, the neighbourhood of the church, were there the positions of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No. They had placed a tanker there at some point, but then they had to pull it out.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when was that when that tanker was there? What year was it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No, I don't recall. I don't know. I think it could have been in 1993 or maybe 1994. I wouldn't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How long was that tank on the positions of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, perhaps about seven days. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And during those seven days, did it open fire? Was it -- was there any fire opened from the tank?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us today that the well was 50 or 60 metres away from your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, I would say I'm not sure how many exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the well to which you went to fetch water, how far from it were the positions and where was the BH army?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, if that's what you mean, they were about 500 metres from our houses, I mean from our neighbourhood. And they were nearer the Serb lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague just reminds me that it is time for the break. Or shall we proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Thank you for assisting me, because I didn't look at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just one Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. thing. I believe we've all noticed it. But for the transcript, when this witness was speaking about the tanker, but the Serb text was "tank." And that is not quite the same thing, is it? So can it be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I noticed that, and in the next line it says "tank" again. So I assume that there will hardly be any confusion. And as you know, overnight still work is done on the transcript. Mrs. Kundo, we'll have a break now for half an hour. And then the cross-examination by Defence will be resumed. So we hope to see you back in half an hour. We'll have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, could you please escort the witness into the Court videoroom. Mrs. Kundo, the cross-examination by counsel for the Defence will now be continued. I see you making some gestures. You can hear me well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, can you tell us where the army of the BH army slept, the army whose positions were 500 metres from your house?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the canteen was?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: For food?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I know where it is, Orahovacka. It's down there on the road. It's the main road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far is that from your house?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, it's quite far. That's the second street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where the headquarters were, or the command post, to which your husband reported for his missions?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of the local commune to which you belonged and under which the Brijesce Brdo Street comes?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: It was called Marinka Bradovica. Or it used to be called Marinka Bradovica, but I don't know what it's called now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which municipality did your local commune belong to?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: It belong to Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far is the police station from your house, or the public security station of the Novi Grad municipality?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: It's quite far. I don't know exactly in metres or kilometres. All I know is that it's quite far.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that on the 2nd of November, on the occasion of the incident that broke out, no one from the Novi Grad Police Station came to see you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: No one came.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence counsel would like to produce an official note, to present an official note. It's a document that the Defence received from the Prosecution. The number is 0028-4045. The Defence has this document in both the B/C/S and in the English version. Bearing in mind the witness's statement that on the 2nd of November no members of the police station came to speak to her, and bearing in mind the fact that she didn't report this incident, this is just for her to confirm that the allegations in the official report are correct. With your permission, I would like to read this out. I have a sufficient number of copies to provide my colleagues with, copies of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you want to tender that document, or just you use it for reading out parts of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I suggest that it be tendered as an exhibit, D75.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a copy in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. With your permission, I will read this out to the witness for that reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can also put it on the ELMO. But given that the witness is not ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see a document on the screen on which in the left-hand side it says, "the Ministry of the Interior, Security Services Centre, Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the date, the 2nd of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that it says "official note"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does it say: "Written on the 2nd of November, 1993, in the premises of the criminal police, for the following reasons"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: "On the 2nd of November, 1993, at about 15.30 hours, sniper shots from the direction of Depo Zeljeznica, she was wounded in the right leg. It was an entry and entrance wound. Kundo Ramiza was wounded, who was born in 1995 and lives in Sarajevo, Brijesce Street, Cikma, number 8"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that but it's not correct. It wasn't my right leg, it was the left leg, but I didn't make this statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. The Defence has no further questions with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just for the French booth, the French booth translated this text as being the left leg, whereas the English booth translated it as right -- as the right leg. And in this text it says the right leg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, Ms. Pilipovic, I do not oppose against tendering the document in evidence because you have presented it to the witness. But the only -- you have read it, and the witness corrected part of it. Is that the relevance for the case, that there's a wrong report? Because when you indicated that you'd present it to the witness, you said that the relevance was that the witness testified that she had not reported anything. Well, of course this letter shows --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still unclear to me because this letter doesn't say anything about reporting anything. It just -- so I don't know. I'm trying to understand what exactly you view the relevance of this document is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence considers that this document is relevant for the Defence, bearing in mind that the witness's statement and she confirmed that she hadn't given a statement to anyone with regard to this incident, and that she had not spoken to members of the police. But that the official note was made on the 2nd of November, 1993, and the witness told us that she wasn't wounded in the right leg but in the left leg. So the Defence considers that this document is relevant for the Defence's case because we believe that this note was not made on that date, and that it wasn't made in accordance with what the witness stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say the imprecision of the document as such is the relevance for your case. Yes, Mr. Ierace, that's a different thing as you indicated prior to reading the document. You didn't say anything about imprecision or ... But we'll see then whether this report will later on turn out to be not a correct one. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me for a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President. The transcript in English for the reading of the document shows that the birth date or the birth year was 1995. The document comes with an English transcript which refers to the birth date as being 1955. When one looks at the original, which is I think still on the ELMO, it appears that there was firstly written 1995 but perhaps there has been a pen mark change to the second "9" to change it to "1955." I simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I take it that this is, apart from a translation, also an interpretation, and I can imagine that someone who draws a report in 1993 will not easily accept that the date of birth of the person injured would be 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It's merely for the transcript, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on the day that you were going to fetch water, were you returning with buckets full of water?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: With regard to the time that you said you were hit, in relation to you at that time, where was your friend who was with you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Well, we were together. I don't know whether she was in front of me or behind me. I'm not sure. I can't remember that exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief today, on page 13, you said that, in response to the question, "Where did you hear the shot coming from," you said that you heard it coming from your right side. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah, I think that was on my right. That must have been on my right. I don't know exactly. I know it was from below, where the Serbian lines were. That's where the snipers shot from.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how far -- on that right side, how far were the Serbian lines from that right side with relation to the place that you were standing?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Maybe about 1 kilometre or 800 metres. I can't say what the exact distance was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the direction that you say came to your right side when you were hit, how far away were the lines of the BH army away from there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Maybe 500 metres. They were nearer to the Serbian lines over there. I don't know exactly. There were two settlements there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us the name of that part of the settlement of which you said that it was to the right of you, and that to the right of you were the positions of the Serbian lines and they were the lines of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: It was the Serbian field. I don't know exactly what it was called. Bacici or something like that. Serbian field, Srpska pole. There was a railway station somewhere there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that your husband was in hospital that day?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which hospital was your husband in?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: He was in Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell him what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I didn't tell him what had happened to me because I was in hospital, and a relative of mine went there to tell him that I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did your husband find out what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: When they took me up to the hospital and I was left there, then my relative and driver went to see him and told him that I had been wounded and that he had to go home because the children were at home and they were on their own.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell your husband what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, when I got out of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell him that you went to the well in the afternoon to get some water and that you had been hit from your right side and in your left leg?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that your husband, with regard to the incident -- with regard to what happened to you, made a statement.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who he gave a statement to?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: I don't know to some policemen I think. I don't know who summoned him, but he was summoned and he gave a statement to the MUP, Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has a statement from Mrs. Kundo's husband. It's a document 0028-4049, and it's dated the 13th of September, 1994. The statement was signed by Mr. Hilmo Kundo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kundo, is that your husband?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation Your Honour, the Defence would like to show part of the statement of the witness's husband.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You want to show it or do you want to read it to the witness, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document can be shown to the witness for her to confirm whether the statement -- whether the signature on the statement is that of her husband. I have a sufficient number of copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please assist Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the statement which was written in the Latin script and has a signature in the left corner - it's signed Kundo Hilmo - be put on the ELMO so that the witness can confirm whether this signature is that of her husband.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you confirm that in the left margin of this document, your husband has placed his signature?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that at the beginning of this statement, it says the 30th of September, 1994?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZA KUNDO
