utterances.text: No, but, Madam Witness, I mean there was only one line of people, or were there several lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many lines. More or less. There were 50 or 60 people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you be more precise and tell us exactly where the pump was located exactly? Could you tell us at what spot in very precise terms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The street is not very wide, perhaps a metre -- perhaps between a metre and a half and two metres. There were three steps there. You go down to the yard. And then it was perhaps 3 or 4 metres from the gate. That's where the pump was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, so the pump was located in the yard or was it in the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes. In the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. In the yard. And you said that the road leading there was a very narrow road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, as we have a transcript in another language which I am reading now, could you remind me of the width of this street? You said that perhaps a metre and a half or two metres. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Witness. I have another question concerning this incident. What did this pump look like? How could one recognise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It was in the earth. There was a pipe which was dug into the earth. There was a pump, a handle, and you would just pump the water out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How high was this pump, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Maybe a metre and a half, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I would now like to, without trying to name the street where this happened, madam, could you confirm how far in metres it was from that street which you have just mentioned and the first areas -- the first airport areas, the beginning of the grounds of the airport? Have you understood my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, I have. But I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, and I'm talking about the initial -- the beginning of the grounds of the airport. Were they far away or were they near the site of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't very far, but it wasn't very near, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, if you know how many streets there were between the street where the incident happened and the beginning of the grounds of the airport -- do you know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Witness, as far as you know, how far -- what was the distance separating the place that we're talking about from the closest front lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Perhaps about 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Madam Witness, as you stated that you stayed for about 48 hours in the line, more or less, I'm going to ask you a question concerning this period of time. Do you know if during this period of time, these 48 hours that we are interested in, a police officer or someone representing the police in Sarajevo came to indicate -- to tell the people that it was dangerous to queue up because it was too close to the confrontation lines? Are you aware of such a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, we were warned by the police -- by our police, but we had to go and get water. I don't know how else one could get by. You had to have water in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, have I understood you well if I consider that the authorities of Sarajevo had warned you of a real risk relating -- which was the result of the proximity of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will repeat it, Madam Witness. You said that the authorities, that is to say, your police, had warned you. Is that correct? Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I see that you agree with that. Thank you. Madam Witness, were you warned of the existence of such a risk? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, was this risk really connected to the proximity of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam Witness, what was this risk related to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, the risk concerned you leaving your house every day. You could be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But, Madam Witness, would you agree with me in saying that you risked being wounded and there was a greater probability of this happening if you were near the line of confrontation or at the line of confrontation, and the risk was greater than if you had been at a distance from this line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I respect that, Witness. I respect that. Witness, I go back to that neighbourhood. Are you aware of some military targets or facilities near the place of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you had lived in Sarajevo throughout the war. Is it that you never heard of a tunnel under the airport, under Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, but there was no tunnel at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you say that the time of that shot, the tunnel was not in existence. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: It was not there. No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So as to make your answer quite clear, when you say "no," are you telling us that a tunnel did not exist at the time? Is that how I should understand you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need to confer for a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, since you tell us that a tunnel was not there at the time, can you tell us when is it that the tunnel in question appeared there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, how can you then be certain whether the tunnel was there or was not there if you do not know since when it was there or when it came to be there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Sir, I know that it had not been built in 1993. When -- I know that it was built eventually, but I do not know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you see in Dobrinja, because that is where you lived, did you see any soldiers of the so-called Bosnian Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Witness, do you know which brigade had its headquarters or was quartered in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, where was the headquarters of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you were aware of the presence of the army in Dobrinja. Did you see those soldiers frequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, these soldiers, did they carry weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Not when they would be walking in the streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did those soldiers wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you, then, into words describe those uniforms? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know where the barracks was or where those soldiers slept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever see any barracks in Dobrinja, military barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: There were no barracks in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, were there any trenches in the proximity of the site of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Perhaps some 50 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you see those trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, who was in those trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: You mean at the time when I was wounded? There wasn't. I couldn't see. I didn't see trenches from there. I simply was aware of trenches around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, I'm asking you generally. In the trenches that you mentioned that were some 50 metres away, who generally was in them during the war, which side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that there were soldiers, madam. But which -- what soldiers? Were they soldiers of the Sarajevo army, the Bosniak army, or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: The soldiers of the Bosnian Army who were defending us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. You said a moment ago that the soldiers whom you saw in the streets were -- did not have any weapons. Are you confirming -- will you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it because they had left their weapons in the battlefield?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, believe me when I say I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, if there was fighting, would it be the principle that the defenders, as you called them, in the trenches, would they be armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, they had to be armed, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, those trenches, did they exist at the time of the incident between -- no -- between the 11th and the 12th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, the soldiers that you saw in the street, where would they be? Where were they going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Well, to the front lines. I don't know. That is my guess. How can I know where they were headed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need two minutes to confer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we would like to suggest to Mrs. Philpott, we have yet another map in reserve, and that is a Sarajevo map, and we would like to show it to the witness so that the witness points out certain things on this map, if that is possible, with your help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Philpott, would you please put the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Your Honour, I have two different maps by the Defence. If they would just indicate which map they would like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you guide Ms. Philpott?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes. I'm sorry, Mr. President. I was confirming. It is a map on which to the right we see a large letter, capital letter, and then words "Novi Grad," new town. And then we see the airport area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, what is the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- at the bottom. We did not mark it. It will be D, but we still do not have a number. We were awaiting to be given a number. I believe that Ms. Philpott has found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Philpott, if you can hear me, with the Chamber's leave, may I guide you? Mr. President, may I guide the registrar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you may do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Yes, Ms. Philpott.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just inquire if there's a copy of that map available for us to see on this side?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is a map that has been used before several times but nevertheless I can imagine that the Prosecution is not prepared. Have you copies, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we shall be very happy to give some copies to the Prosecution. But that is indeed the map that has been used very often. I do not know if we can have a clearer image because I'm afraid it is rather vague. No, my screen is quite dark, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's a matter of fact it's the light in Sarajevo put on the -- I think it's becoming clear now, but now too clear. Somewhere -- yes, this is, I think, the best we had until now. Would you have copies for the Chamber as well, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't think that we can get it any clearer than this. But I am going to ask Ms. Philpott that she puts -- that she moves up this map slightly so that we can see the airport area. Yes. Can you put it up? Very good. I think this is it. Just a moment, Mr. President. Right. I believe now that we have this area. Thank you very much, Ms. Philpott. I believe we have Novi Grad here in the upper part -- upper right part of the screen. And then down diagonally the runway of the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see this map in front of you over there in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you make out what it says? Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why, Witness, can't you read this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Because these are not my reading glasses. I have to look for another pair of glasses in my handbag. If I may just get another pair of glasses. Then I'll be able to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We shall ask to blow it up -- to blow up this image in Sarajevo. I do not know if you can do it, and tell us if you can read it then or not. And then we shall ask the technical booth to zoom it as much as possible. There. Stop. Stop. Stop. Thank you. Stop. Witness, can you read it now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yeah, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the technical booth now move it to the right. [In English] Move it slowly to the right. Stop. Stop. Stop. Stop. Stop. [Interpretation] Slightly to the -- [In English] Right again, please. No. A little bit more to the right, please. This way, this way, this way. That's the left. Move it to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you have to be clear on whether the map has to be moved or the camera has to be moved to the right, because that gives a different effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] I was talking about the image, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] The only way that this is possible is if the map is moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Would you please move, [Interpretation] Ms. Philpott, so that we can see the lower right part of the Sarajevo airport, please. There. And slightly to the left, now. This whole exercise seems to be very difficult. Ms. Philpott, can you please move it to the left so that we can see both the top of the airport and the bottom of the locality of Dobrinja? Can you manage to do that? I will ask the technical booth to once again that they reduce the image on the screen because I believe it will then be easier and then we should be able to zoom in on the particular spot. Now, will you move the map to the right, please, Ms. Philpott? There. There you are. Just a little bit more, please. Thank you. Thank you. That will be fine. Technical booth, can you now zoom in the area -- stop, stop. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you point -- perfect. Witness, can you please point now at the area where the incident happened. Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I can't. I can't read this. I can't find my way about it. I know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, is it that you do not understand my question, or is it that you can't get your bearings on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I can't get my bearings here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you see, and I'm not asking you any names but can you see a bulevar which I believe is called Mimar Sinana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you see it? And in relation to that, do you know it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, then do you see this bulevar which you don't know, a street which I think is -- I think it says Louis Posteur.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No, it's Louis Pasteur.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Oh, yes indeed. So sorry. Yes, Louis Pasteur Street. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in relation to that street, can you identify the street where the incident or incidents happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I suggest in the interests of economy of time that we could agree to the location where the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the parties could agree upon that, we don't have to ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- which is marked using the latest technology, and the tunnel marked with various places -- if we could agree on that map, then perhaps we could move very quickly in respect to the location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was in relation to these kind of exercises that the Chamber invited both parties to present a map. We haven't received it yet, but would there be a possibility, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to compromise on the location of the incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I think so. But what we can do, I will guide the witness so that we can see if that is it. But the problem is not so much the problem of the tunnel now that we are concerned with. About that, we can agree. But it's those trenches which the witness said were 50 metres away, and I thought that the witness could then point to them on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you may continue questioning. But I do remind you, just in order to have an idea on what problems we might encounter in assessing the probative value, that the witness has three times said already -- well, more or less that she can't read maps. At least, she can't find her way on this map. So but please proceed, but please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, on this map that you have before you, as it is now positioned on the screen, do you see in the lower part of the image which represents the built-in part, do you read a number 153? Can you see those three figures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No. Oh, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, Witness. Witness, since you see that, this street that is below the street called Louis Pasteur, was it more or less the site of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: Believe me when I say that I don't know because I simply don't understand. I cannot read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. Can you then, on this map, and this will be my last question to do with the map, can you point at two things: one, the existence of trenches? Can you do that? Can you tell us their position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. And this tunnel that you know was not there, allegedly, in July 1993, do you know where it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No re-examination from the Prosecution. Mrs. AE, you've by now answered all the questions of the parties, and the Judges have no additional questions for you. That means that this concludes your examination as a witness. I'd like to thank you very much for having come to the courtroom, although it's at a distance in Sarajevo, the video courtroom, and I hope you understand that it's important for this Chamber to hear the testimony of those who were present at these times, your testimony answering questions of Prosecution and answering questions of the Defence. So I once again would like to thank you very much. And Ms. Philpott, the witness may be led out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that we will deal with the documents tendered in relation to this last witness perhaps also on Monday morning, and perhaps I've got two questions in relation to it. The first one is whether the map is going to be tendered in evidence or not. I leave it up to the Defence, but I don't know whether you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't think so. Like the last time, the witnesses cannot read. So it wouldn't serve any purpose. There will be no sense in tendering a text which was -- a document which has not been addressed by the witness or marked by a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This brings me to an observation. Could -- and for the future, it's also addressed to the Defence but also at this moment particularly to the Prosecution, that they invite witnesses to bring all glasses that they possess so that we have the best chance of getting the information that we are seeking. Then, to the Prosecution, it's a relatively short document that you intended to tender. That's P3365.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. If I may briefly address the Court on it, I have been informed that specific provisions have been made and are available for the Defence to request retranslations or further translations, and I think the reason I'm being informed of it is, as I remember now, that we had been specifically guided, if I may put it that way, or perhaps directed, by the previous Trial Chamber seized of this case, that because of the expected amount of cases which would start in this Tribunal in this year, that the official translation unit should not be asked to translate the entirety of any document presented to them, only those parts considered to be relevant. Any party would be free, if they thought that sufficient quantities were not translated, or there was a mistranslation, to require a full translation or a retranslation. And I say so because it may well be that having regard to the huge amount of medical documentation that they would have had to translate, they might well have been instructed to stick to the diagnosis, unless they were requested by any party to go into other parties. But I do recall that the previous Trial Chamber had directed that only matters considered to be relevant to the issues should be translated, and the parties should refrain from translating every single item on a document unless an issue was raised. That is the observation I make. However, regarding the fact that the issue has been raised now as to the further writing, I will do what my friend could have done, I will ask the translation unit to translate those further three lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first ask whether the Defence, having looked at this document now, insist on having translated the parts that were not translated yet, and then perhaps indicate exactly what should be translated. Because I didn't hear -- in the cross-examination, I have not noticed specific attention for this document and for those parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are resisting, especially from what we heard from my learned friend, and this is for the following reasons: Every time, and you have seen it, every time when a medical document is produced, there are problems which had to do with the translation. And we are simply wondering if this is not a strategy aimed at exhausting the Defence which all the time runs behind the translations so as to be able to do its very basic work. So that we say this is as a matter of principle. If I did not raise this question during the cross-examination, Mr. President, it is simply that I have no medical knowledge, and that even if we can see what penicillin is, the rest we just do not know what and so forth. We are not medical experts, and unlike the Prosecution, and therefore I do not know what questions to ask, and we do not want to waste time. But we cannot accept this. Either the documents are translated or they are simply not translated, and therefore not produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I ask you what exactly what part, because you can read them more or less. I see that "amnecia, diagnocici" [phoen] something, well, that's preprinted. That seems to be translated. Then in the translation, we find the word "shrapnel wounds, visible wounds as stated above." Is that the translation of just the first handwritten line or the first and the second handwritten line as far as you can identify at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see, Mr. President, it seems that the entire part that starts more or less with "MA" which in the margins of the document, all of this where they mention the toilets and of cleaning the wound, et cetera, as far as I can understand, this part has not been translated, apparently because it is illegible. But it's not illegible. For once, it's perfectly legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll consider this. So we see that up until Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. "MA," everything is translated in your view. Yes? Okay. Perhaps we'll deal with it after the weekend, so we can consider it. Apart from that, I think we have dealt with all the issues we have to deal with. But Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if I said that -- what I said was not translated. I see that you said everything would be translated. What I said is that this was not translated. I don't think that that was clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I said everything up to where it reads "MA" has been translated, and the rest has not been translated. Yes. No misunderstanding about that. We'll then -- we have finished, I think, all videolink witnesses in Sarajevo. So next week, apart from the documents we have to decide upon whether they will be admitted in evidence or not, there's nothing else to be discussed at this very moment. So we'll adjourn until next Monday morning, 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2.33 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 25th day of March, 2002, at 9.30 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
